data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 answers the panel-vs-expert comparison but never addresses the problem's second, decisive requirement: identify the evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. Its mechanism is all about LLN/variance reduction and 'expert blindness,' and its counterconditions are about when the panel fails, not about how to tell a real gain from coincidental compliance in the data you actually have. A counterexample: an evaluation where the panel scores higher on the objective outcomes exactly as SRC_001 predicts, yet every item was solved by rote box-ticking that tracked the key without the panel understanding why. Under SRC_001's own definitions this would count as the panel outperforming the expert, so it cannot separate the genuine gain the problem asks about from the compliant mimicry it warns against.
